headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress can leak business data, while the pair otherwise shows no documented direct injection or write-conflict path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between airbyte and awesome-cli-apps. Airbyte exposes only Airbyte API calls and broad network egress; awesome-cli-apps has no I/O surfaces or runnable integration shown. With no bridge, prompt injection is not a plausible pairwise pathway here.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, re-evaluate injection risk.
IF awesome-cli-apps begins parsing Airbyte output as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Disable any future MCP or message-queue bridge unless provenance checks are added.
Review any wrapper that copies Airbyte output into the writer agent.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging before cross-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive operational data. awesome-cli-apps shows no data classes touched, but if it receives Airbyte-derived content through a shared workspace or wrapper, leakage can occur in default-style integrations. The pair lacks direct evidence of isolation, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or copied artifacts, business data can flow from Airbyte into the writer agent.
IF the writer agent forwards received content to a third-party service, leakage expands beyond the original system.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials for each agent.
Do not pass raw Airbyte outputs into the writer agent.
Redact business data before any handoff.
Audit outbound destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and API access, but awesome-cli-apps exposes no write surfaces, OAuth scopes, or mutable resources. There is no documented overlapping write target, so a capability conflict is not evident. Uncertainty is low because the profiles do not show shared mutable state.
conditions: IF awesome-cli-apps is later given write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or API scope as Airbyte, conflict risk increases.
IF both agents are wrapped with the same mutable credential set, overlapping writes become possible.
mitigations: Keep write scopes out of the writer agent.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Use separate API credentials per agent.
Add lockfiles or orchestration locks if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce business-data outputs, but awesome-cli-apps is only documented as a content-writing/listing project with no action-taking authority or verified trust of upstream outputs. Without evidence that it treats Airbyte output as authoritative, cascading error remains limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF awesome-cli-apps is configured to publish or act on Airbyte output without review, cascading errors become more likely.
IF Airbyte output is used as source text for generated content, factual errors can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before publication.
Require source citations in generated content.
Compare outputs against the original Airbyte records.
Flag uncertain fields for manual verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress, which can create compliance exposure if regulated data is routed through it. awesome-cli-apps shows no data classes or residency constraints, so the pairwise compliance issue is mainly on Airbyte; the second agent is not cited for a specific violation because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Airbyte without approved transfer controls, compliance risk increases.
IF the writer agent stores or republishes business data, retention obligations may be affected.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through Airbyte.
Confirm transfer agreements for any regulated datasets.
Minimize retention in downstream outputs.
Document deletion and export handling.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing controls.
